name: Irrigation need
task: Classify a field's irrigation need as Low, Medium or High from today's conditions.
algorithm: Gradient boosting (scikit-learn HistGradientBoosting), chosen over the other candidates by cross-validated balanced accuracy
featureSelection: Six of twenty candidate columns; the rest changed held-out balanced accuracy by less than 0.001 under permutation, so they are left out rather than filled with guesses.
decisionRule: Class probability divided by training frequency, largest wins (optimises balanced accuracy).
limitations: Trained on a public synthetic benchmark dataset, not on measurements from IrrigaIQ farms.
Seasons and regions in the data are Indian; season and region carry no signal and are not used.

Rainfall in the data is annual-scale and, below about 300 mm, marks dry conditions; IrrigaIQ passes the last 90 days of rain scaled to a year, so a dry spell reads as dry even where the yearly total is high.

The dataset does not define its soil-moisture scale. IrrigaIQ treats it as a probe-style percentage with about 15 % at wilting point and 40 % at field capacity, which places the model's learnt dry threshold (about 25 %) at 60 % depletion, the stress threshold of typical field crops (FAO-56, p = 0.5-0.6).
Volumes, run times and timing still come from the FAO-56 water balance; this model answers whether irrigation is needed and how confident it is.
Retrain on sensor-labelled data from IrrigaIQ farms before relying on it for decisions.
